Thanks for the ping — read ACME's redlines. Commercially my preference is a middle-ground: 45-day opt-out for pilot accounts only, and TfC allowed but with a capped fee equal to 25% of remaining committed monthly charges (or 60 days of forecasted minimums), whichever is lower. Also propose a documented wind-down period of 30 days during which we provide export and transition support (same as our offboarding SLA).

Why this works:
- 45-day gives ACME some runway while retaining our forecast edge vs. 30-day.
- A capped fee protects us from full loss while still offering ACME a safety valve for pilots.
- Limit the carveout to Order Form IDs (pilot-XXX) so it does not become a company-wide term.

If Laura can draft precise redline language that ties the pilot carveout to a single Order Form and excludes any inference into the MSA's main termination-for-convenience clause, we should be in decent shape to present to their counsel.

Karthik Iyer

Draft legal position below — I've kept it narrow and operational to avoid establishing precedent in the MSA. Suggested wording for an Order Form addendum (redline ready):

"Termination for Convenience — Pilot Order Forms: Notwithstanding Section X of the MSA, for Order Forms expressly labeled 'Pilot' (Order Form ID prefixed with PILOT-), Customer may terminate the Pilot Order Form for convenience by providing Redwood with at least forty-five (45) days' prior written notice. Such termination shall be subject to either (i) payment of a termination fee equal to the lesser of twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining minimum committed fees under the Pilot Order Form or an amount equal to sixty (60) days of the then-applicable minimum monthly charges, or (ii) a mutually agreed pro-rata settlement for consumed services during the wind-down period. Redwood's obligations to provide transition assistance and export of Customer data shall continue for a period of thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination."

Operational controls to protect us from precedent risk: include a clause that the addendum "applies solely to the specific Order Form and does not amend or otherwise modify the MSA or any other Order Form unless expressly agreed in writing by authorized signatories of both parties."

If ACME pushes for 30-day opt-out, we should escalate to VP of Sales for a discretionary concession tied to a Managed Services premium or reduced pilot credits. I can prepare the redline and include the limiting clause.

Laura Bennett
Senior Corporate Counsel, Redwood Inference

Jared / Marta — thanks for the clear ask and for the redline. We talked through this with commercial and legal. Below is a consolidated proposal intended to protect both sides while keeping the pilot program flexible: 

1) Notice window for pilot Order Forms: 45 days (applies only to Order Forms explicitly labeled PILOT- in the Order Form header).
2) Termination for convenience: allowed for pilot Order Forms with a capped fee equal to the lesser of 25% of remaining committed fees or 60 days of minimum monthly charges. Alternatively we can take a pro-rata settlement for consumed usage during the 30-day wind-down.
3) Transition assistance: Redwood will provide export + transition support for 30 days post-termination (per our offboarding SLA).
4) No MSA amendment: the pilot carveout will be documented in an Order Form addendum that does not change any other MSA terms unless explicitly signed by both parties.

Next steps: Laura will upload the redline addendum; Karthik and I recommend signature if this aligns with ACME's needs. We can send the DocuSign link once you confirm.
